name: Bubble Break ASMR
request: Create a small, playable Bubble Break ASMR game for one player on desktop and touch. The player presses individual bubbles on a reusable bubble-wrap sheet. A press visibly depresses and pops that bubble with synchronized satisfying pop audio, then adds exactly one to the popped counter after the pop completes. Holding, spamming, or pressing a popped bubble must not count twice. Let the player finish a sheet of at least twelve bubbles, see completion feedback, and deliberately reset to a fresh sheet. Use a close, readable tabletop presentation and minimal counter/reset UI. Search Marketplace first for a complete reusable interaction, including any existing geometry, animation, sounds and behavior; inspect what it already provides and integrate only missing features. Search separately for missing media if needed. Audio must come from Marketplace and actually play. Record unavailable importer capabilities rather than pretending a suitable scripted component does not exist. Choose reasonable details yourself; no saving, multiplayer, purchases or large map. Success needs observed press/pop/recovery timing, per-bubble state, exact counting, sheet completion/reset and usable desktop/touch input. Do not claim success from code inspection alone.

assetNeeds.role: A complete reusable bubble-wrap popping system or interactive model that may supply the sheet geometry, independently targetable bubbles, existing press/pop animation, state transitions, input behavior, reset behavior, and embedded sound references.
assetNeeds.constraints: Search complete interactive systems before static props. Prefer at least twelve individually readable bubbles in a compact sheet suitable for a close tabletop. Inspect all included scripts, dependencies, remotes, animations, constraints, sounds, input paths, count/reset behavior, and licensing/provenance metadata. Desktop and touch suitability must be demonstrated. Retain useful verified behavior and media. Unsupported script, animation, rig, package, or serialization capabilities must be recorded and escalated rather than used to justify a procedural replacement. Do not execute numeric require IDs or arbitrary HTTP code.

intent.experienceRole: This component is the physical and behavioral centerpiece of the ASMR loop, letting the player methodically finish and refresh a tactile sheet rather than interact with a merely decorative prop.
intent.interaction: The player clicks or taps one available bubble; it visibly depresses, pops with synchronized audio, settles into a popped state, and permits exactly one delayed count award. Finishing all bubbles triggers completion feedback, while reset is a separate deliberate action.
reusableFeatures: Per-bubble available, pressing, and popped state
Press, depression, pop, and settled animation timing
Embedded pop sound references and emitters
Counter, completion, and reset behavior or signals

assetNeeds.role: Marketplace-provenanced satisfying bubble-pop audio for the exact visible pop moment, sourced first from retained component media and searched separately when that component has no suitable verified sound.
assetNeeds.constraints: Prefer a clean, close, short pop without speech, music, clipping, or long ambience. Preserve Marketplace provenance. The asset must load, play, and be heard in native Roblox review at an appropriate non-startling level, and must synchronize with the visible pop completion event. Captured audio from the retained complete component has priority. No generated, procedural, built-in, placeholder, or invented-ID fallback is permitted.

intent.experienceRole: The audible pop provides the central ASMR reward and confirms the exact transition from depressed to completed bubble.
intent.interaction: Audio plays once for each accepted fresh bubble at the visible pop moment, before the corresponding count increments; rejected, held, duplicate, stale, or already-popped inputs produce no additional pop sound or reward.
reusableFeatures: Existing emitter or spatial playback setup

spec.assetStrategy:
Begin with Marketplace Model discovery for a complete bubble-wrap interaction, not a static sheet. Inspect candidate hierarchy, scripts, interfaces, animation data, input behavior, independent bubble state, debounce, completion/reset handling, and embedded sound references before deciding what must be authored. Preserve any verified geometry, behavior, animation, and media that directly serve the requested loop; unrelated systems are omitted without damaging dependencies. Because exact imported interfaces are unknown, discovery-dependent integration tasks intentionally own no script paths until inspection establishes the smallest necessary glue and exclusive ownership.

The pop-audio obligation is declared separately even when a complete component includes sound. Audio captured from the retained component is reviewed first; separate Marketplace audio search occurs if no suitable included sound survives provenance, loading, playback, listening, and synchronization checks. Standalone animation retrieval is not assumed. If a candidate relies on unsupported animation, scripts, rigs, packages, serialization, numeric require IDs, or other unavailable importer capabilities, record the exact capability gap and escalate it; do not silently rebuild or claim that no suitable scripted component exists. Native Roblox verification is mandatory before accepting interaction, media, timing, desktop/touch usability, or presentation claims.
spec.title: Bubble Break ASMR
spec.summary:
A compact, single-player bubble-wrap popping experience for desktop and touch. The player spawns immediately beside a close tabletop station with the bubble-wrap sheet centered in view, a small popped counter, and a clearly labeled reset control. The first available bubble provides the obvious action: click or tap it, observe a short press/depression phase, hear a synchronized Marketplace-sourced pop, then see that bubble settle into its popped state as the counter increases by exactly one. The player continues across a sheet containing at least twelve individually tracked bubbles. When the final pop finishes, the sheet presents calm, readable completion feedback without automatically resetting. The player deliberately uses Reset Sheet to restore every bubble and return the counter to zero.

The playable space is one bounded tabletop interaction area rather than a large map. Its landmarks are the safe spawn/viewing position, the central bubble-wrap sheet, the counter, and the reset control. The sheet remains within comfortable close-range interaction distance and is framed so individual targets are readable without travel. Server-owned state validates bubble identity, availability, distance, timing, rate limits, completion, and reset requests; the client is responsible for cross-device input and presentation. No saving, multiplayer systems, purchases, progression, combat, or unrelated exploration are included.

Marketplace discovery and source inspection occur before implementation ownership is finalized. A complete reusable bubble-wrap interaction must be sought first and audited for geometry, bubble state, input, animation, recovery, sounds, and reset behavior. Verified useful content is preserved, and only demonstrated gaps receive integration work. Included or separately discovered audio must be loaded, played, and listened to in Roblox. Unsupported script, animation, rig, or importer capabilities are recorded as blocked review gaps rather than treated as authorization to replace the component. All interaction, timing, audio, touch, completion, and reset claims require native gameplay observation; code inspection alone is insufficient.
spec.visualDirection:
Use a close, softly lit tabletop composition with the bubble sheet as the dominant focal point. The table should have a warm, low-contrast matte surface; the sheet should use cool translucent or pearlescent material cues so bubble silhouettes remain distinct. Arrange at least twelve bubbles in a tidy rectangular grid with generous separation and consistent size. Unpopped bubbles should read as rounded and raised, an actively pressed bubble should visibly compress, and a completed bubble should remain flatter and slightly less luminous or saturated without becoming invisible.

Keep the camera and spawn relationship intimate and readable: the player should face the sheet at a shallow overhead angle, with the entire grid visible while individual bubbles remain large enough for reliable touch targeting. Use a small authored tabletop boundary or backdrop to contain the composition, avoid visual clutter, and ensure the spawn surface is collidable and safe. Lighting should favor soft highlights on bubble domes and gentle shadows that make depression depth apparent.

The HUD should be minimal: one compact popped count such as “Popped 0 / 12,” one deliberate “Reset Sheet” button, and a restrained completion message. Keep controls away from the bubble grid, use high-contrast text, rounded panels, and touch-safe target sizing. During a pop, combine geometric depression, brief highlight/material response, and synchronized audio; update the count only after the observed pop completion point. On finishing the sheet, use a short celebratory pulse or glow and a clear “Sheet Complete” message while leaving reset under player control. Reset should visibly restore the whole grid and return the presentation to its initial calm state.

tasks.title: Search Marketplace for complete bubble-wrap interaction systems, inspect candidate hierarchies and sources, and retain the best verified reusable component without stripping embedded behavior or media.

Audit pop sounds captured from the retained component first; if none satisfy the requirement, search Marketplace separately and verify provenance, loading, playback, audibility, and synchronization suitability.
Compose the bounded tabletop station, safe spawn/viewing relationship, lighting, interaction clearance, and sheet placement around the retained component's verified dimensions.

After component inspection, map retained interfaces to authoritative bubble state, pop-completion signals, count updates, reset generation, input, HUD, and audio; record capability gaps and assign only the necessary glue scripts.
Integrate only the missing server-authoritative press, per-bubble transition, post-completion count, validation, completion, reset, and cleanup behavior established by inspection.
Integrate missing desktop/touch targeting and the minimal persistent counter, reset, and completion presentation against the inspected component and authoritative state interfaces.
Tune the retained or integrated depression, pop, settled-state, reset, completion, and synchronized sound presentation while preserving verified Marketplace animation and media.

Run protected native desktop and touch verification of the complete sheet loop, timing, audio, state validation, exact counting, completion, reset, respawn, cleanup, and tabletop readability; report gaps honestly.
